S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.normalized_text: For probability measures P and Q on a common measurable space, their total variation distance is \operatorname{TV}(P,Q):=\sup_{B}|P(B)-Q(B)|=\frac{1}{2}\int|p-q|\,d\lambda, where the supremum ranges over measurable sets, and p and q are the densities of P and Q with respect to any common dominating measure \lambda. In particular, |\mathbb{E}_{P}h-\mathbb{E}_{Q}h|\leq\operatorname{TV}(P,Q) for every measurable function h taking values in [0,1].

A2.SS2.SSS2.p4.normalized_text: For every Q\in O(n), conjugation preserves Haar measure and the determinant sign, while A_{QOQ^{\top}}=QA_{O}Q^{\top} and p_{QOQ^{\top}}(Qx)=p_{O}(x). Consequently, for every x\in\mathbb{R}^{n}, \mathbb{E}[\det(O)p_{O}(x)]=\mathbb{E}[\det(O)p_{O}(\|x\|e_{1})]. At \|x\|e_{1}, the Gaussian exponent depends on O only through U, since e_{1}^{\top}A_{O}e_{1}=(\kappa+1-(\kappa-1)U)/2. Moreover, I_{n}\preceq A_{O}\preceq\kappa I_{n} gives the integrable bound h_{\lambda}(x)p_{O}(\|x\|e_{1})\leq\left(\frac{\kappa}{2\pi}\right)^{n/2}e^{-\|x\|^{2}/2}. Using |\det(O)|=1, Fubini’s theorem, and Gaussian integration, we obtain \displaystyle H(\lambda) \displaystyle=\frac{1}{(2\pi)^{n/2}}\mathbb{E}\left[\det(O)\sqrt{\det A_{O}}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{n}}e^{-[\kappa+1+4\lambda-(\kappa-1)U]\|x\|^{2}/4}\,dx\right] \displaystyle=2^{n/2}\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{\det(O)\sqrt{\det A_{O}}}{(\kappa+1+4\lambda-(\kappa-1)U)^{n/2}}\right], where \int_{\mathbb{R}^{n}}e^{-a\|x\|^{2}/4}\,dx=(4\pi/a)^{n/2} for a>0. The denominator is at least 2+4\lambda, so Lemma B.6 applies with h(u)=(\kappa+1+4\lambda-(\kappa-1)u)^{-n/2} and gives H(\lambda)=\frac{(-1)^{n-1}(\sqrt{\kappa}-1)^{n-1}}{2^{n/2}}\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{(\sqrt{\kappa}+1)U-(\sqrt{\kappa}-1)}{(\kappa+1+4\lambda-(\kappa-1)U)^{n/2}}\right]. (21) Since Oe_{1} is uniform on \mathbb{S}^{n-1}, Lemma A.1 applies to U.

A2.SS2.SSS2.p6.normalized_text: It remains to lower-bound the test gap. Since n/2\geq 1, convexity of t\mapsto t^{n/2} implies \left(1-\frac{1}{n}\right)^{n/2}\geq 1-\frac{n}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{n}=\frac{1}{2}. Also, \displaystyle n(1-r^{2}) \displaystyle=\frac{4n\sqrt{\kappa}}{(\sqrt{\kappa}+1)^{2}}+\left(\frac{\sqrt{\kappa}-1}{\sqrt{\kappa}+1}\right)^{2}\left(2-\frac{1}{n}\right) \displaystyle\leq\frac{4n\sqrt{\kappa}}{(\sqrt{\kappa}+1)^{2}}+2. Together with Eq. (20) and Eq. (24), these estimates give \displaystyle\operatorname{TV}(P_{+1},P_{-1}) \displaystyle\geq\frac{2}{n}\left(\frac{\sqrt{\kappa}-1}{\sqrt{\kappa}+1}\right)^{n}\frac{(1-1/n)^{n/2}}{1-r^{2}} \displaystyle\geq\frac{\left(\frac{\sqrt{\kappa}-1}{\sqrt{\kappa}+1}\right)^{n}}{2+\frac{4n\sqrt{\kappa}}{(\sqrt{\kappa}+1)^{2}}}. This proves the first claimed bound. For the second, \kappa\geq 4 implies \displaystyle\log\left(\frac{\sqrt{\kappa}+1}{\sqrt{\kappa}-1}\right) \displaystyle=2\int_{0}^{1/\sqrt{\kappa}}\frac{dt}{1-t^{2}} \displaystyle\leq\frac{2}{\sqrt{\kappa}(1-\kappa^{-1})}\leq\frac{8}{3\sqrt{\kappa}}\leq\frac{3}{\sqrt{\kappa}}. Hence ((\sqrt{\kappa}-1)/(\sqrt{\kappa}+1))^{n}\geq e^{-3n/\sqrt{\kappa}}. Using 1+t\leq e^{t}, we also have 2+\frac{4n\sqrt{\kappa}}{(\sqrt{\kappa}+1)^{2}}\leq 2+\frac{4n}{\sqrt{\kappa}}\leq 2e^{2n/\sqrt{\kappa}}. Therefore, \operatorname{TV}(P_{+1},P_{-1})\geq\frac{e^{-3n/\sqrt{\kappa}}}{2e^{2n/\sqrt{\kappa}}}=\frac{1}{2}e^{-5n/\sqrt{\kappa}}. ∎
